sentence_stem: There was hardly any milk in the fridge, so
correct_completion: we bought some more at the shop.
full_sentence: There was hardly any milk in the fridge, so we bought some more at the shop.

options.text: we had a big glass of milk.
options.why_wrong: 'So' introduces a result of the first clause. A big glass of milk does not follow from having hardly any milk.

options.text: we did not need to buy anything.
options.why_wrong: This contradicts the cause. Having hardly any milk creates a need to buy more, not a lack of need.

options.text: we bought some more at the shop.
the fridge was empty and cold.
options.why_wrong: This repeats the description of the fridge but does not give a result of the cause stated before 'so'.

grammar_focus: Quantifier 'hardly any' with a cause-and-effect connector 'so'
explanation: The word 'so' shows a result. The first clause says there is almost no milk, so the completion must describe what people did because of that shortage.
translation: Casi no había leche en la nevera, así que compramos más en la tienda.
